# 1 Enoch Chapter 14 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 14 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 14:8 — heavenly transport imagery — 'clouds invited me' vs. 'clouds beckoned'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "clouds invited-me and-a-mist summoned-me" | Literal Ge'ez: clouds and mist as active agents issuing an invitation |
| LOGOS | "clouds called to me and a mist summoned me" | Personification preserved; 'called' more natural than 'invited' |
| PNEUMA | "clouds beckoned, mist called to me" | Terse, evocative; 'beckoned' captures the visual gesture |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'clouds called to me and a mist summoned me' (LOGOS). The Ge'ez uses two verbs of summons — the parallelism should be preserved. PNEUMA's compression loses the second verb. EMET's 'invited' is too social/polite for a theophanic summons.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Stylistic — parallelism in theophanic language.

---

## 14:13 — 'hot as fire and cold as ice' — the paradox of the divine house

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "hot as-fire and-cold as-ice: there-were no delights of-life therein" | Literal rendering; 'delights of life' for Ge'ez term |
| LOGOS | "as hot as fire and as cold as ice. There were no comforts of life in it" | 'Comforts' better English for the Ge'ez concept of livable conditions |
| PNEUMA | "furnace-hot and ice-cold at the same time. There was nothing in it to comfort a living being" | Intensified metaphors; 'comfort a living being' makes the inhuman nature explicit |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. The paradox of simultaneous fire and ice signals a reality beyond normal physics — the divine realm transcends human categories. 'Comforts of life' is a good balance. PNEUMA's 'furnace-hot' adds specificity not in the Ge'ez.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. The paradox is theologically loaded — divine transcendence.

---

## 14:20 — 'the Great Glory' — divine epithet translation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-Great-Glory" | Literal: Ge'ez kebra 'ab'iy — the Great Glory as a divine title |
| LOGOS | "the Great Glory" | Same; treats it as a proper epithet |
| PNEUMA | "the Great Glory" | Same; all three agree this is a title, not a description |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** All three agree: 'the Great Glory' is preserved as a divine epithet, capitalized. This is one of the most important Enochic titles for God — it avoids the divine name while emphasizing the visible manifestation of God's presence (cf. Ezekiel's kavod). No divergence on this verse.

**Status:** Unanimous. Key Enochic divine title.

---
